name: Ahab
overview: Ahab was a male king of Israel, uniquely identified as the son of Omri and noted for his reign marked by profound wickedness. According to Scripture, he did more evil in the sight of the LORD than all the kings before him, provoking God's anger extensively. His leadership is remembered as a significant negative turning point in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahab means 'brother of father,' a proper name recorded in 1 Kings 16:28. He also held the titles 'King of Israel' and 'King of Samaria,' reflecting his political authority over the northern kingdom. These titles emphasize his role as the ruling monarch during a turbulent period in Israel's history.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ahab as the son of Omri and the husband of Jezebel. He is also understood to be the father of Joash, Ahaziah, Jehoram, and Athaliah, indicating a dynastic lineage that continued his royal legacy. These relationships are documented in various passages within 1 and 2 Kings.
scriptureSignificance: Ahab's reign is significant in the biblical narrative because it exemplifies the consequences of persistent disobedience to God. His actions, more provocative against the LORD than any previous Israelite king, highlight the dangers of forsaking God's commands. His story serves as a sobering example of the spiritual decline that can accompany ungodly leadership.
